definitions.explanation: A large, elegant wading bird with long legs and neck. Cranes are symbols of longevity and good fortune in Japanese culture.

examples.japanese: {北海道|ほっかいどう}では{丹頂鶴|たんちょうづる}が{見|み}られる。
examples.english: You can see red-crowned cranes in Hokkaido.

examples.japanese: {千羽鶴|せんばづる}を{折|お}って{病気|びょうき}の{友達|ともだち}に{贈|おく}った。
examples.english: I folded a thousand paper cranes and gave them to my sick friend.

examples.japanese: {鶴|つる}は{長寿|ちょうじゅ}の{象徴|しょうちょう}とされている。
examples.english: Cranes are considered symbols of longevity.

notes:
{鶴|つる} refers to cranes, particularly associated with the red-crowned crane ({丹頂鶴|たんちょうづる}).

Common expressions:
- {千羽鶴|せんばづる} (thousand paper cranes - folded for wishes/recovery)
- {折|お}り{鶴|づる} (origami crane)
- {鶴|つる}の{一声|ひとこえ} (the voice of authority; a decisive word from the top)
- {鶴|つる}は{千年|せんねん}、{亀|かめ}は{万年|まんねん} (cranes live 1,000 years, turtles 10,000 years - wishes for longevity)

Counter: {羽|わ}

Cultural note:
The {丹頂鶴|たんちょうづる} (red-crowned crane) is a national symbol of Japan and appears on the logo of Japan Airlines. {千羽鶴|せんばづる} became internationally known through the story of Sadako Sasaki, who folded paper cranes while hospitalized after the Hiroshima bombing. Cranes symbolize longevity, good fortune, and fidelity.
